title: US-Iran: Trump's Decision Day on Resuming Strikes; CNN/CBS Live Coverage of Deal Negotiations; Core Issues: Uranium Stockpile, Sanctions Sequencing, Hormuz Transit Fees
detail: May 24, 2026 is Trump's self-declared decision point on whether to resume military strikes against Iran's nuclear program or accept the draft peace framework. CNN and CBS News ran live updates throughout the day on the Iran-US deal negotiations. The deal under discussion covers three primary elements: first, the disposition of Iran's enriched uranium stockpile — approximately 400–460 kg at 60% purity, which Iranian Parliament Speaker Qalifbaf and the negotiating team discussed relocating or capping as part of a temporary agreement; second, a framework for sanctions relief sequencing tied to verified enrichment curtailment; and third, Strait of Hormuz transit fee arrangements to manage the reopening of the waterway that has been blocked for approximately 12 weeks, trapping approximately 750 vessels and causing the most significant global shipping disruption since Suez. The CBS News live tracker covered real-time developments as the US-Iran peace process entered its most consequential 48 hours since the April 10 ceasefire. Pakistan's Army Chief General Asim Munir continued as the key intermediary connecting the US principals (Witkoff, Kushner, Vance) with the Iranian side (Qalifbaf coordinating with Supreme Leader Khamenei's office). The Week India reported that a 60-day ceasefire extension was the most likely near-term outcome — providing diplomatic runway to negotiate the substantive nuclear parameters: enrichment duration (US demands 20+ years; Iran offers 5; 12-year compromise foreclosed by May 14 congressional letter); enrichment level ceiling (US demands zero domestic enrichment; Iran insists on enrichment rights); and IAEA monitoring access. The global economic stakes include a $3–4/barrel oil price premium due to Hormuz closure, approximately $6 billion in monthly Iranian oil export revenue blocked, US domestic gasoline at $4.48/gallon (highest since July 2022), and significant global shipping rerouting costs. Lebanon remains on day 8 of its 45-day ceasefire extension as the Pentagon security track approaches May 29. Colombia's election is 7 days away. The Iran-US deal — if finalized — would reshape the entire Middle East diplomatic landscape.
